lines.text: Meet ChargeOne. Plan an electric road trip across India, with charging stops you can trust.

No sign-in to start. Type your car's chassis number, and ChargeOne recognises it. Every model is built in 3D from the real car's dimensions, in its own factory colours, with its real battery and range.
ChargeOne offers a free week of Plus. Or stay on Basic, which is free for everyone.
The map opens on a 3D globe, and flies you down to India.
Tilt it into 3D, with real hills and terrain. Chargers glow where drivers say they're working.
Tap a charger to see if it's available or occupied, from drivers' reports. One tap opens the operator's own app, to start charging and pay.
Sign in, and one tap starts your free Plus week.
Connect your car. This is the demo car, clearly labelled. It rolls in, switches its lights on, and shows live speed, power and battery.
Car makers don't share connected car data with other apps yet. So ChargeOne uses your phone's GPS, or a Bluetooth OBD adapter in beta, which can even recognise your car by itself.
Plus members get a trip co-pilot. Ask it by voice, in Hindi or English.
कोयंबटूर से चेन्नई जाना है, बैटरी साठ प्रतिशत है।
कोयंबटूर से चेन्नई का प्लान बना रही हूँ, बैटरी साठ प्रतिशत।
It draws and compares up to three routes: the fastest, the one with more fast chargers, and any that aren't safe on your battery.
Start the drive. The map follows you in 3D, and your battery forecast for every stop updates live.
If the battery drains faster than planned, ChargeOne warns you early, and offers a charger before the one you planned.
One tap switches to it, and the plan updates.
Basic is free for everyone. Plus adds the co-pilot, live drive alerts and car connection, with seven days free. Coming first to Google Play.
